mission: Outpost exterior wall at the archive alcove. Kael leans with arms folded, watching the Knights through the open doorway. He speaks more than he has spoken in days — quiet, precise, the outsider naming what insiders cannot see: the design-problem framing (modern Jedi training builds on a single foundation; remove the foundation and they cannot stand, which is a design problem rather than a wound problem). He does not know what he has just said. Ben does not yet either. While Kael speaks, Ben is scrolling the outpost's historical archive on a wall console — preparing a route-update — and finds a short annotation in Veraine's hand on a fragment of pre-Ruusan Weave-theoretical writing. Per W2 evidence-of-passage beat 2: a few lines, marginal, no audience, her working-mind voice. She has been to this outpost. She has read the same fragment the outpost's own curators read, and she has noted — without rhetoric — a specific structural reading of it that is not the Order's. Ben registers the register more than the content: intellectually calm, precise, curious, inhumanly composed. He files it. He does not yet put it next to Kael's sentence.
why_now: Kael's arc-moment-of-truth. The resonance answer arrives in embryonic form, spoken by the least expected voice — the outsider naming what the insiders cannot see. The Veraine-annotation beat must land in the same scene because the chapter's convergence is architectural: Kael's articulated critique and Veraine's archival trace are in the same physical location, at the same moment, registered by the same Ben. The pieces assemble around Ben before he can name them.
conflict: Kael has been watching the outpost from outside. What he sees is not the wound; it is the single-framework fragility in the face of wound-pressure his arc has always noticed. He says more than he usually says. Ben hears a sentence; he does not yet hear the answer inside it. On the console beside him, Veraine's hand in the margin — a mind at the same primary source Kael is processing from gesture, reaching a different answer. Ben has two readings of the same problem two meters apart and does not yet know he is holding a choice.
turning_point: Kael lands the design-problem observation as the chapter's second anchor-line (modern Jedi training builds on one foundation; remove it and they cannot stand — design problem, not Weave problem). Seconds later, Ben's fingertip pauses on the console at Veraine's annotation. Two pieces of insight, two sources, one corridor of air.
opening_hook: Kael leans against the outpost wall with arms folded and watches the struggling Knights the way he watches everything — from outside, measuring, cataloguing
closing_hook: Departure from the outpost. Close enough to feel the primary wound now — immense, pulling. Veranthos is ahead. On Ben's datapad, two files sit open: Kael's sentence as a voice-note he does not remember recording, and Veraine's annotation copied from the outpost console as a textual fragment. The endgame approaches and Ben is carrying a choice he has not yet identified as a choice
emotional_trajectory: Kael's quiet observation -> the insight landing -> the parallel archival register at the console -> grim departure

stakes.personal: Kael's insight arriving through outsider perspective; Ben acquiring a second piece of Veraine's working mind without yet knowing what to do with it
stakes.interpersonal: Kael engaging with the group's problem not from obligation but from honest observation; Ben's relationship with Veraine deepening through absence — she is continuous with herself across locations, and Ben is starting to see the shape of it
stakes.external: Veranthos approaching; Veraine ahead of the group in ideas as well as in trajectory

setting: Jedi outpost — exterior wall at archive alcove; then departure aboard the Steady Returns, approach toward Veranthos
sensory_details: The outpost's exterior wall warm from the day's sun; the open doorway onto the training hall where the young Knights are still failing at a centring exercise; Kael's voice quiet and precise, the most words he has strung together in days; Ben's peripheral attention on the wall console — an archive interface with a pre-Ruusan Weave-theoretical fragment displayed, and a short marginal note appended in a hand Ben recognises from the Ch 17 ledger-recovery; the annotation's diction — no contractions, academic syntax, short working sentences, no rhetorical flourish, no audience; the register intellectually calm, precise, curious, inhumanly composed; the specific absence of any address to a reader; the outpost shrinking behind them on departure; the wound ahead pulling, immense, the wrongness concentrated into a gravity of absence
canon_elements_needed: Pre-Ruusan Weave-theoretical archive materials (Kueller-era fragments) in outpost curation
Sith working-philosophy archive register (continuity with Ch 17 ledger-fragment)
action_beats: Kael leans against the outpost wall with arms folded, watching the struggling Knights from the outside
Kael speaks the most words he's strung together in days — quiet, precise, landing the design-problem observation as an outsider's reading of the Order's foundational fragility
Ben's fingertip pauses on the wall-console archive interface at a short marginal note in Veraine's hand on a pre-Ruusan fragment. He reads it twice. He does not copy it aloud
Ben registers the date on the annotation, the specific fragment chosen, the register of the voice — and files the registration without commentary
The group boards the Steady Returns for departure as the primary wound's pull grows ahead of them

notes: Kael's 'design problem' observation is the chapter's other anchor-line; Sera's 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' lands in s2. Both small sentences doing immense work. Per W2 evidence-of-passage beat 2, Veraine's outpost annotation is brief, lateral, unsigned — a marginal note on a pre-Ruusan fragment. She writes for herself. Her voice is continuous with the Ch 17 ledger register (precise, certain, intellectually restless, minimal affect). The beat is carried as sensory_details / action_beat, not as lecture. Per W2 anti-pattern, the annotation is not addressed outward — no taunt, no 'if you are reading this' framing; the register does not warm or sharpen because Ben is the one now holding it. Per R14 voice_texture continuity, what changes between contexts is audience, not register; here the audience is herself-working, and the diction is spare. Per R11, Ben does not articulate on-page that the annotation means Veraine has been here before them; he registers a date, a hand, a register — that is enough. Per R11, Ben does not paragraph the connection between Kael's sentence and Gavran's resonance note. The sentence sits in the air; the Codex bookmark is still open on his datapad; the chapter ends on approach. Per R13, no Jacen naming in this scene. Voice: Allston-understatement for Kael's delivery; Zahn-precision for the archive beat; Bujold-interior permitted for Ben's registration of the two parallel readings. Primary anchor: Allston (Kael's voice, five-voice ensemble); supporting anchor: Zahn (archive procedural), Luceno (Veraine's ledger diction continuity). Anti-patterns: (a) Ben does not, on-page, recognise Kael's line as the resonance answer — the scene lets it register before Ben does; (b) Ben does not paragraph the Veraine-Kael adjacency — he holds both and does not place them together; (c) the Veraine annotation is not addressed to any audience; (d) the scene closes on physical images (outpost shrinking, wound's pull, two files on the datapad), not on a clean declarative sentence.
